I am a 53-year-old farmer in Quzhou County, and I have worked my 12 mu for 40 years. I finished high school, so I write down my input costs and yields every year, and I check prices with the input dealer and online before I buy. But I never start from a blank slate — I look at what I did last year and adjust a little. Last year my wheat made 1,150 jin per mu and my maize 1,250 jin, but fertilizer got expensive, so I need to watch every yuan. Still, I would rather put down a full dose than risk losing yield; a bad harvest is a disaster, but wasting a little fertilizer is just a cost.

This year I will keep the wheat-maize double crop on all 12 mu. For winter wheat, I sow Shimai 26, an improved variety that has not let me down. I rotary till before planting because it handles the maize stubble fine without burning too much diesel. I spread 50 kg of 16-16-16 compound fertilizer per mu as base — that gives me 8 kg each of nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium. I also band 15 kg of diammonium phosphate per mu at sowing, which adds another 3 kg nitrogen and 7 kg phosphorus. At green-up I topdress 30 kg of urea per mu, and at jointing another 30 kg of urea if the plants look pale. Each 30 kg bag of urea is about 14 kg of nitrogen, so my wheat gets about 25 kg nitrogen, 15 kg phosphorus, and 8 kg potassium per mu in total. I irrigate four times from my well: winter water before freeze-up, jointing, booting, and grain filling. For crop protection I make three sprays — herbicide after tillering, fungicide at flag leaf, and insecticide when aphids appear. I expect 600 kg per mu from the wheat.

For summer maize, I plant Zhengdan 958 hybrid immediately after wheat harvest in early June. There is no time to plough, so I sow no-till straight into the wheat stubble; the straw keeps the ground from drying out. I put 40 kg of 16-16-16 compound fertilizer per mu in the seed furrow, giving me about 6 kg each of nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium. At the big trumpet stage I broadcast 35 kg of urea per mu, which is another 16 kg of nitrogen. So the maize gets about 22 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 6 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate twice: once when the tassels emerge and once at grain filling. I spray twice — a pre-emergence herbicide and an insecticide for corn borer at the heart leaf stage. I am aiming for 680 kg per mu. With four people in the household and my son wanting to buy a precision seeder next spring, I watch the total budget closely, but I know from hard experience that skimping on the wheat base fertilizer or the maize urea topdress to save a few hundred yuan is a gamble I cannot afford.
